items.title: Charles "Creole Charlie" Levy Interview, 1962-01-03
items.q: And then we played the tunes of the day, like Tartle in Chicago, you know. We played those things.

ctx.x: And you had the blues, all the famous New Orleans type of...

Yeah, we had, we played, well, see, the man that we were going to feature in the blues, he picked these keys. He said, all right, the blues and B flat. Now, maybe that, that, we wouldn't live, Klan, most of that. Well, all right, that was his blues. All right, trumpet player, he, maybe he played his blues and concert E flat. And we'd play that, and he'd take it for his own. He'd take the circle of course, and then finally some of them, I'd play blues on the violin, and somebody would answer it. And, in other…
I suppose that was often a piano feature.
